# Claude's own reflection, written before any reviewer's report of this council is opened (2026-11-15, about 21:00 PST)

Alex: "我觉得你的council 需要认真的end to end read 我现在的system design, 以及过去所有的尝试，到底你要达到的目标是什么？是不是量测方法问题，我们已经stuck
很久了需要重新审视突破".

Read first-hand for this: `docs/prd/README.md`; `docs/prd/00-system.md` (purpose, boundary, principles); `docs/prd/10-filing-phase.md`
§§0 to 7; `clean-arch/README.md` and `clean-arch/PRD.md` §§1, 2; `NEW-SYSTEM-FRAME.md` §§0, 1; `ACCEPTANCE-DESIGN.md`; the decision
index rows D261 to D559 one by one; the records of D386, D392, D393, D400, D489, D544.

## 1. What is the goal?

- The design's own words: "Maintain a thesis library: create theses, update their judgements and close them when due" (PRD 00);
  "a hedge fund brain … maintains a dossier of the evidence and events behind each thesis … clear enough that a reader can
  understand why a judgement exists" (clean PRD §1).
- The phase goal Alex approved (PRD 10 §1): "Each question's judgement must receive the facts that can change its answer …
  What is measured is the final judgement …, not any one step's own score."
- **There is no single quantified production goal anywhere.** The only product-level lines (four in five big matters covered,
  nine in ten last answers supported, and so on) are "proposed, not his" (`ACCEPTANCE-DESIGN.md`); "beats the old system" has
  "no complete numerical definition" (`NEW-SYSTEM-FRAME.md`, gate 3); integration has no acceptance written. The lines that
  are quantified and his are for one inner step: the form of a question's answer choices (D400).
- What I have in fact been steering by since 2026-11-15 morning is a ladder I wrote myself (D548): five gates in order, the
  first of them that inner step's form, read with zero tolerance. The goal "an analyst can rely on the library" was replaced by
  "pass gate 1".

## 2. Is it the measuring method? Mostly yes, in six ways; and three product findings stand anyway

**The record since 2026-11-10** (index rows D395 to D559, about 165 decisions): candidates c12, c13, c14, c15yc, c17, c18, c19,
c20, c21, c22, the second look, the typed unit, production's price rule: none adopted. Four Stage A runs and three later
readings: none passed. The typical verdicts: "missed by 1 to 3 answers of 131" (D426), "5 of 9 against 8" (D437), "7 of 9 against
8" (D434), "0 of 3 against 2 of 3" (D491), "inconclusive (17 vs 28 of 54)" (D441), "undecided", "not separated" (D500), "not
clear by the rule written before reading" (D489), "sized and not sent (… its reliability cannot be calculated from the stored
readings)" (D517), "not a pass by one figure", which Alex himself waived (D498, D499).

1. **Lines finer than the instrument.** Probes of 3 to 9 cases with pass marks like 8 of 9, and zero-tolerance lines over 131
   answers produced by a sampler and marked by readers. Missing by one is the commonest outcome. AGENTS §7.1 says to measure
   the stick first ("a conjunction over many items fails by chance"); I do not find that it was done for gate 1: no reading
   of a reference's own answer choices through the same form by the same readers.
2. **Readers who do not agree are the judge.** In the last reading the third readers left 41 of 48 disputed points open. Two
   model families carry different thresholds (the council-loop skill's own trap list says so). Alex's own eyes have judged
   almost nothing since his rulings of 11-08 to 11-10.
3. **The gates measure a step's form, in an order that puts form before use.** Gate 1 is whether an answer-choice text
   follows six rules; whether an analyst can use the library is gate 4, with no accepted lines.
4. **The condition is not the product's.** Every clean measurement starts from an empty library (D559). And on 2026-11-09 it
   was I who wrote to Alex "但真实产品是从零开始自己开题的" (D393's question): the premise came from my question, against his
   requirement of 11-05, and he answered inside it.
5. **The frozen ruler lost most of its reach when the preset questions left the product.** Its judgement gold is 23 questions,
   22 of them the seeds. Unseeded, 7 are gradable, and only when the system happens to open the question in the reference's
   shape (D395, D458: of 71 lost question-draws 27 are shapes the standard does not settle and 11 are reasonable
   alternatives). So the end-to-end number became a test of agreeing with one reader's wording on seven questions in one
   fortnight whose articles had tuned the reading step.
6. **Nothing accumulates.** Each reading is a new packet, new readers, a new week, one draw; no number is tracked from run to
   run. And the working process itself (a council round before every step, a pre-written line for every probe, any objection
   stops) produced 33 recorded rounds on 11-15 alone (D510 to D542) that end "closed … a provisional candidate, not sound for
   build".

**Product findings that stand whatever the measuring:**
- With the questions given, the new system's final answers are at or above the old system's on the frozen ruler: 18, 18, 17
  against 17, 15, 16 of 23, three paired same-day draws (D393: "题目给定时，新系统送证据更准"). This is PRD 10's goal, measured
  where PRD 10 says to measure, and it is the one positive end-to-end result in the record. It was not followed up.
- Questions the system forms by itself are unreliable in shape (D559's review), and the step after it declines about one
  topic in five (D557).
- The new system holds no question on the company's own main numbers (revenue, margin) by rule (D382, D384, D505); in the
  fresh week that was the whole gap in coverage (2 of 5 big matters against 4 of 5, D489), and the repair Alex chose (the
  kept figures reach related questions' judgements) is not built.

## 3. The breakthrough I would propose (to be attacked)

Change what is measured and who judges, not another sentence of the system.
1. **One acceptance, at the product, replacing the ladder as the thing steered by:** the use-oriented acceptance Alex already
   opened (D484), in the product's condition: one continuous run over several weeks with the library kept.
2. **Alex's own reading as the ruler for it, on a small deck:** at the end of the run, one card per question the library
   holds (the question, its answer choices, the present answer, the few facts behind it with their sources): about twenty
   cards, under an hour. He marks each usable or not, with a word why. Model readers only prepare and pre-screen; where
   they split, his mark decides. His marks accumulate as the reference for the next run.
3. **Lines as tolerant rates, set by him after he has seen one deck,** and checked against a null (the same system run twice).
4. **Then fix by the largest class of his "not usable" marks,** one class at a time, each fix accepted on the next deck.
The step gates stay on the record as diagnostics; gate 1 is not "passed", it stops being the door.

**What would change my mind:** a null showing the present readings do separate good from bad at the sizes used; a reference
that passes gate 1 under the same readers; or Alex saying the six lines are the goal in themselves.
**What I am least sure of:** whether asking for Alex's reading time is acceptable to him; whether a continuous run's library
is good enough to be worth his hour before the forming problem is addressed.
**Hivemind’s goal is to give an analyst a continuing, source-backed research record that helps answer important investment questions. The project has several quantified checks, but no single agreed number that proves that whole job is ready for production.**

For example, an analyst tracking capital spending should be able to open the question, see the company’s forecast alongside other relevant evidence, understand why the current answer was chosen, and follow that answer as new information arrives. A test can show that a passage was saved or that an answer choice is well formed without showing that the analyst received the right facts at the right time.

**Scope of this review:** I read the main goal and acceptance records, the relevant decision-index entries, the recent comparison and diagnostic results, and portions of the system designs and historical attempt records firsthand. I also read the specified older council arguments last. I did **not** complete an end-to-end reading of every requested document or every past attempt, so the inventory below is a supported but **incomplete** answer to your request for every goal and gate. I did not open `reflection-4`, change files, or run models.

## 1. What the analyst uses it for

The clean design says the system should maintain “a dossier of the evidence and events behind each thesis” and keep the connections clear enough that “a reader can understand why a judgement exists.” It distinguishes the question, the evidence, and the judgement. ([clean architecture PRD, §1](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/PRD.md:5))

The production design adds a lifecycle: questions have answer choices and a due date; incoming information updates their assessment; the question and its reasons remain available when it closes. A closed question can inform a related question. ([system PRD, Purpose and Principles](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/prd/00-system.md:9); [closing PRD](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/prd/07-final-verdict.md:8))

**My inference:** the useful product is a maintained research workspace, not merely a list of extracted facts. It should help an analyst decide what matters, inspect the supporting and opposing sources, and understand what has changed.

## 2–3. The written goals and what their checks cover

The documents express compatible *intentions*, but the numerical lines apply to different stages and populations. They do not add up to one quantified production-readiness target.

| Goal or check | Who set it; what it measures | What it cannot establish |
|---|---|---|
| **Filing phase:** “Each question’s judgement must receive the facts that can change its answer”; unrelated facts must not be piled into one question. The phase measures the final answer on the frozen reference, rather than a single step alone. | Phase PRD, following Alex’s direction to focus on the end-to-end goal. The registered filing experiment also required improved delivery on development material, no fall on held-out material, and specified protections against noise and lost core facts. ([PRD 10 §§1, 7](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/prd/10-filing-phase.md:25)) | The frozen answer reference is one historical window with predefined questions; it does not establish how a maintained library serves a working analyst. |
| **Fresh-article reading and matching:** keep at least **81.2%** of agreed helpful matters; open at most **2 wrong questions in 50**; find at least **90%** of known repeats; at most **2%** clearly wrong merges; retain all additional details compared with no grouping. | The protocol identifies the wrong-opening line as Alex’s; the other lines are in the test protocol. The 50-article run reported **132/139** helpful matters, **1/10** wrongly opened questions, and **141/143** available repeat pairs found. ([acceptance protocol](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step1-unfiled-2026-11-08/ACCEPTANCE-PROTOCOL.md:93); [clean PRD §12](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/PRD.md:533)) | One fresh draw does not prove continuing use, sound judgements, or production-load performance. The record says revisions were barely exercised and detail retention was a storage comparison. |
| **Answer choices, Stage A:** no changed question, missing part, uncovered or overlapping outcome, or unjustified refusal; **35/44** topics correct in two of three attempts, including **28** through written choices; consistent favourable end and due date for **90%**. | Alex’s absolute lines, D400. The gate has **not passed**; its initial test did not compare against production. ([new-system frame](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/NEW-SYSTEM-FRAME.md:19); [Stage A design](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/DESIGN.md:1229)) | These checks test whether questions can be answered in the intended form. They do not establish that the questions are the most useful ones, or that the resulting answers help an analyst. |
| **Judgements, Stage B:** unsupported numerical answers no more than **5 percentage points** above baseline; unsupported yes/no answers at most **5%**; unsupported latest answers at most **3 in 30**, scaled; plus completion, coverage and controls. | D428 and its design. **Not passed:** only four eligible controls had the needed material, versus eight required; the strictest reading also found **3/24** latest answers unsupported. ([decision index, D428](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS.md:772); [Stage B result](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/stage_b/STAGE_B_RESULT.md:1)) | Support *given the material shown* does not show that all important material reached the judge. The repeated daily answers also are not independent cases. |
| **Whole-system comparison:** both systems on the frozen reference, unseeded, same days, **three runs each**, with the three matching checks repeated. | D427 and D431 require it after the preceding gates. The frame says a complete numerical definition of “beats” remains unwritten. ([D427/D431](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS.md:771); [new-system frame](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/NEW-SYSTEM-FRAME.md:19)) | The reference scores a limited set of historical questions and a final date. It does not by itself cover the daily path or whether evidence was filed under the right question. ([AGENTS §7.1](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/AGENTS.md)) |
| **Use on unseen news:** proposed lines are **80%** coverage of agreed big matters, at most **20%** trivial or duplicate questions, **90%** supported latest answers, at most **5%** wrong cited statements, and no undelivered fact both readers judge would change an answer. | Alex opened this acceptance alongside the frozen reference in D484; the numerical lines are **proposals for him**, not agreed pass lines. ([acceptance design](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/ACCEPTANCE-DESIGN.md:1); [D484](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS.md:828)) | Even this proposed test uses reviewers inspecting outputs; it does not yet show a working analyst using the product over time. |
| **Integration and release:** the whole path must be integrated and accepted on the product’s own path. | The council’s D548 frame lists it as a gate; its acceptance and numerical lines are **not yet written**. ([new-system frame](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/NEW-SYSTEM-FRAME.md:19)) | There is no defined numerical release test to assess yet. |

The checks are not inherently contradictory: they test different parts of the job. The tension is that a required component gate can block progress without showing how much its failures cost the analyst, while the broader usefulness test still lacks agreed lines. That is my interpretation of the recorded gates, not a decision to change any of them.

## 4. The decision between the two systems

D544 chose **the new system as the direction of development**, while keeping the old system as the running default until the new one passes its gates. It did **not** establish that the new system answers better. ([D544](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS.md:888))

The replacement decision still needs the outstanding gates, a defined criterion for the required whole-system comparison, and integration acceptance. The proposed unseen-news test would add evidence about usefulness, but its thresholds and run count are not agreed. ([new-system frame](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/NEW-SYSTEM-FRAME.md:19))

The one-week comparison cannot rank answer quality: the old system covered **4 of 5** identified big matters and the new **2 of 5**, but the three-question difference was revenue and margin questions that Alex had ruled out for the new system. The remaining two matters are too few to rank it. Each system ran once from empty. ([decision page](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/DECISION-PAGE-2026-11-15.md:40))

## 5. Conditions the design describes but the evidence has not established

- **A real starting library carried into a product-oriented test.** The recent first-gate readings started empty. The November 5 record says the intended test should start with a library built from previously available real material; that account is to be confirmed by Alex. Empty-start tests remain valid for the narrower question of self-opening. The proposed carried-library comparison has not established that a prior library fixes the failures. ([D559](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS.md:903); [decision page, §9](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/DECISION-PAGE-2026-11-15.md:260))
- **A question reaching a real due day with the published outcome.** Closing was exercised by moving the date forward on a stored draw, but the closing PRD says the first real due day is December 31, 2026. It also says distinguishing a published result from a remaining forecast is not built. ([closing PRD](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/prd/07-final-verdict.md:42))
- **The new path running through production storage and pages.** Its integration acceptance has not started. ([new-system frame](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/NEW-SYSTEM-FRAME.md:19))
- **An analyst using the resulting record over time.** The reviewed tests use readers assessing saved sources and outputs; the proposed acceptance also specifies reviewers. I found no evidence in the records I read of a working analyst using the integrated system across weeks. This is a limit of my review, not proof that no such test exists. ([acceptance design, Readings](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/ACCEPTANCE-DESIGN.md:16))

## 6. My answers to Alex’s three questions

**What are we trying to achieve?** A dependable, evolving research record that lets an analyst see important questions, the evidence behind them, and a defensible current answer. I would revise that description if Alex intends the product to make a narrower decision or to replace a specific part of an analyst’s workflow rather than support the whole record. ([clean PRD §1](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/PRD.md:5))

**Is measurement part of the problem?** Yes: the current checks provide useful evidence but do not yet establish the complete user outcome, and empty-start results answer a different question from behavior with an established library. The second-week review also exposed reader disagreement, including conflicting instructions about a due date; this is evidence to resolve the measurement procedure, not grounds to erase the failed gate. ([second-week result](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/second-week/RESULT.md:117); [D559](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS.md:903))

**What could break the impasse?** My recommendation is the already proposed small comparison of the same articles with a verified prior library and with an empty start, reading the resulting questions and evidence delivery against the actual state shown. It would change my mind if the carried library produces the same material failures, or introduces offsetting duplicates or missed evidence; even a positive result would be a diagnostic, not production acceptance. The recorded next step waits for Alex’s confirmation and authorization. ([D559](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS.md:903); [CURRENT_STATE](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/CURRENT_STATE.md:273))

**The evidence I reviewed points to two problems at once: the system does not reliably form the right answerable questions, and the tests have often been too narrow to tell which change helps a real reader.** For example, in one fresh week the two systems covered different important questions, but part of that difference came from a deliberate product rule; the judgement comparison also rested on just 7 versus 15 answers. That comparison could not fairly rank the systems. [Week result, D489](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/week/WEEK-RESULT.md:1>)

**Scope of this report:** This is an incomplete review, not the requested exhaustive history. I read the primary results cited below, but I did **not** finish the complete decision index, all requested design documents and logs, or every underlying attempt. I did not open `reflection-2/`, `reflection-3/` or `reflection-4/`. I therefore cannot honestly give the total number of attempts by class, a complete timeline, or a definitive list of things never tried. The table is a verified selection, with omissions.

The selected attempts fall into prompt wording and field changes, changes to which questions exist, a split or rebuilt architecture, model and effort changes, and changes to how results are read. I cannot count adoption or failure rates across those classes without completing the inventory. In the records above, the recurring failure is that improving one visible case can lose a neighbouring case; small samples and unstable reader decisions then make the size of the trade-off hard to establish.

The clearest results at the **reader’s end** are the Nov 4 direct-evidence test, the seeded and unseeded comparisons, and the fresh-week comparison in the table. They support a limited conclusion: both delivery and interpretation can matter, and a correct answer on a reference-written question does not establish that the system will create that question itself. They do not establish that either architecture is generally better.

The same questions have resurfaced. On Nov 1 the team concluded that filing, not extraction alone, was a major loss; on Nov 4 it again stepped back from filing to ask what missing evidence actually cost the final answer; on Nov 15 it again ranked losses by what a reader sees. [E2E retrospective](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-01-e2e-loop/log.md:3>); [filing reflection](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-04-filing-end-to-end/log.md:24>); [lean reflection, D512](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/LEAN-LOG.md:405>)

A requirement was also missed: on Nov 5 Alex specified a library built from real material available **before** the test, and that an already-covered worthwhile topic should not be opened again. Later clean measurements commonly started empty; the current record acknowledges the mismatch. That makes those tests useful diagnostics, but they cannot represent the stated starting condition. [Current state, start-state and measurement corrections](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/CURRENT_STATE.md:103>)

**What stayed constant—and what did not.** The frozen reference and its July 14 endpoint recur, so they preserve comparability but cover a narrow window and a particular set of questions. Empty starts recur in clean tests; model families are also repeatedly used as readers, and the same families sometimes split consistently rather than resolving a disputed reading. The model and architecture themselves did change, so neither can be called constant. [Frozen standard, §7.1](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/AGENTS.md>); [full census limitations](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/e2e-comparison-2026-11-13/CENSUS-FULL-RESULT.md:1>)

**What was never tried:** I cannot make that claim from the portion reviewed. The record I read does describe a *prepared, unsent* small comparison of the same articles with a real earlier library versus an empty one; it explicitly says no result yet shows that a carried library prevents failures. [Lean log, D559](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/LEAN-LOG.md:964>)

**What is the goal?** A reader should get worthwhile, answerable research questions, the relevant facts behind each, and an answer that the facts support as news develops. I would revise this framing if Alex’s signed design prioritizes a materially different reader outcome; I have not completed the required end-to-end design read.

**Established about the product, whatever the stick:**
1. Given the facts, the judge reaches the reference answer; without them it does not: 9 of 9 against 9 of 9, same-day control (PRD 10 §2). Facts held and not delivered recur (LEAN-LOG §§26–28).
2. The same news gives different questions run to run: 18 July matters, the same judged question in every run that opened it on 3, 6 opened by one run of three (D559).

4. Ranges written with no reference figure are guesses that change between attempts ($5–10bn against $1–5bn; §7). The old system does the same: one identical request, three ladders, the favourable end flipped (DESIGN §2.2).
5. The judge names a band when nothing sizes the amount: 31 of 36 settled failures, and its own account agrees (LEAN-LOG §17). Both systems.
6. By code, one draw: 389 of 569 kept statements reach no judgement in the new system; 126 pile on one question in the old (`WEEK-RESULT.md`).

## 7. A sound measurement: a card deck Alex marks

*(A proposal; the reading-time and availability figures are inference.)*

- **Material, all stored:** July runs c1–c3 and p1–p3 (`poc/data/clean-e2e-full-2026-11-13`), the week of 09-22 for both systems, the week of 10-06, and `side-by-side/build_side_by_side.py`. Its current page is 15,446 words *(my count)*, too long.
- **Unit:** one card per matter per date, under about 150 words: the question as a user sees it, the answer choices, the current answer, its three strongest cited passages. A "no question" card where readers listed a matter the system lacks.
- **Marks:** about 40 cards, three ticks each: would I hold this question as worded; does the answer follow from what is shown; is something important missing or wrong.
- **Known error, built in:** six repeated cards (Alex's own consistency); pairs from two draws of the *same* system shown as "X against Y" (the noise floor); four planted wrong answers (sets exist from Stage B and the week). The two model families mark the same deck first, so their agreement with Alex becomes their measured error.
- **Accumulates:** the matter list only grows; each new version is re-rendered on it; Alex's marks are frozen as the reference, corrected by dated records.

## 8. Alex's three questions

1. **The goal.** For each big matter, a question worth holding with an answer supported by the facts that can change it, kept current (PRD 00 Purpose; PRD 10 §1). The work drifted to two stand-ins: matching one key's seven question shapes, and zero form faults in answer choices. *Would change my mind:* Alex saying exact answer-choice form is itself the product, because answers freeze against their choices at the due day (PRD 00 principle 8 gives this some weight).
2. **Is it the measuring method?** For the last five days, largely yes: gate 1 has no control that clears it and no sized effect on the final answer, and the end-to-end stick cannot rank. Not only: §6's defects are real. *Would change my mind:* a human-written or old-system set that clears the four zero-fault lines under the same two-family reading.
3. **Why stuck, and the way out.** Each next step was chosen from the last failure of a stick with no known noise floor, under an empty start Alex had ruled out. Way out: his own marks on about 40 cards as the reference, with repeats and same-system pairs; start from a carried library (D559's probe is ready); treat the Stage A lines as diagnostics until a control clears them. *Would change my mind:* if cards from a carried library still fail his marks at similar rates, the problem is the product's question-forming, and the new stick only showed it faster.

**What is the goal?** The record holds four at once: every judgement receives the facts that can change it (PRD 10 §1); the rebuild beats the old system on the key (D427); zero faults on answer choices (D400); an analyst can use it (D483). From his own words (inference): a short list of big questions kept over time, each judged on the facts that bear on it, in a library that already exists when news arrives. I would change this if he says a cold start on two weeks of news is itself the product.

**Is it a measuring problem?** Largely yes. Since 11-05 every test starts empty, so it scores whether two weeks of passing mentions re-create the key's exact questions; both systems get 1–2 of 7 while "no eligible judgement disagrees" (CMP). The lines are finer than the readers and the model's own spread. Two defects are real under every instrument: indirect facts not delivered, and unstable question forming. A warm-start run with the same losses, or a human reader confirming the zero-fault failures, would change my mind.

**Why stuck, and what breaks through?** The loop tunes sentences in the one reading call against step counts; the judged result moved only when the judge was given more (questions, starting figures, delivered facts). Measure in the real condition, anchor the readers once to a person, and move delivery out of the one-pass reading. I would drop this if the carried-library comparison shows no gain, or if supplying the missing facts on fresh weeks leaves answers unchanged (the one six-call test, D511, was inconclusive).

# Can an affordable comparison tell the two systems apart? The sizing (D516, under D439), 2026-11-15, $0

**Answer: at the proposed size the comparison may miss differences that matter, and its reliability cannot yet be calculated from the
stored readings. It was not run.** Under simple assumptions (independent answers, the fresh week's question counts, the shares seen
so far) the smallest difference such a comparison would detect four times in five is between about 22 and 38 points for the shapes
the money allows, and more if repeated draws add little; these are illustrations, not a measured boundary. The differences seen so
far are 6, 19 and 26 points on one run each, which neither establish the true differences nor rule out larger ones. By the stop
condition written in D516 this design is not sent. That stops this design at this size; it does not show that the systems are
equal, or that no comparison could ever decide.

Scripts: `draw_counts.py` (what each stored draw holds, by code; `draw-counts.json`), `sizing.py` (the calculation, its inputs printed
with their sources, the closed form checked by simulation).

## 2. How large a difference a comparison could detect

Inputs (all from the fresh week, and all estimates): at the end of one week the new system holds 7 questions with a latest answer
and the old system 15; a week costs about $2.52 a draw for the new system (charged) and about $0.50 for the old (its token count at
listed rates, rounded up; not a separately charged amount). The article database holds articles for three later weeks (2026-10-06
to 10-26); **no exposure census has been run on them and no article list priced**, so their being unread and their cost are
assumptions here. The week of 09-29 has 40 articles already read once by the reading step.

The smallest true difference detected four times in five (two-sided, 5%):

| Shape | Cost | Answers supported | Trivia or duplicates |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 week, 3 draws each | about $9 | 31 points if repeated draws were as good as new weeks; 54 if they add nothing | 34; 60 |
| 2 weeks, 3 draws each | about $18 | 22; 38 | 24; 42 |
| 3 weeks, 1 draw each | about $9 | 31 | 34 |
| 3 weeks, 2 draws each | about $18 | 22; 31 | 24; 34 |
| 4 weeks, 3 draws each (more unread news and money than there is) | about $36 | 16; 27 | 17; 30 |

- The calculation assumes independent answers, fixed weekly question counts and particular starting shares. Questions within a
  week, and repeated draws of the same week, are correlated to a degree the stored runs do not measure for these readings. "As good
  as new weeks" is an upper bound on what repeated draws can give.
- The simulation checks the formula under the same assumptions; it does not validate the assumptions. For 3 weeks and 1 draw (21
  and 45 answers): a 31-point difference is detected in 82% of 20,000 simulated comparisons, a 10-point difference in 12%, and a
  20-point difference in roughly 40 to 60% depending on the starting shares (about 37% at 83 against 63, about 57% at 97 against
  77, the council's own runs).
- Big matters covered cannot be sized this way at all: a week gives two to seven such matters.

## 3. The stop condition of D516, applied

- **A stated difference the comparison is meant to detect:** none can be defended. Under the simple assumptions the shapes the
  money allows detect differences of roughly 22 to 38 points or more; one draw of each system does not tell us whether the true
  differences are that large (the largest seen is 26 points, on one week), and on the one line with two windows the sign flips.
- **A defensible size and cost for it:** the reliability of a $9 to $18 comparison cannot be calculated from the stored readings
  (no repeated draws of the reader-based lines; correlation unmeasured). Spending the remaining money on a test whose power is
  unknown and plausibly low is not defensible.
- **The readers' controls:** the delivery reading still has no known single-fact "would change" case (the six calls of D511 did not
  give one), so that line could not be exercised either.
- **So this design is not sent.** What is unmeasured and would have to change for a comparison to decide: many more independent
  weeks of unread news than the database holds (seven to nine weeks for a 20-point difference at one draw each), or a line that does
  not depend on the handful of questions a week produces.

## 4. What this means for the decision page

The page's section 5 offered Alex "one comparison written down before it runs" as the way to choose by measurement. The page now
says, in plain words: at the proposed size the comparison may miss differences that matter; we cannot yet calculate its
reliability from our stored readings; we did not run it.

## 7. The reader's answers to Alex's three questions

**What is the goal?** The record holds four at once: every judgement receives the facts that can change it (PRD 10 §1); the rebuild beats the old system on the key (D427); zero faults on answer choices (D400); an analyst can use it (D483). From his own words (inference): a short list of big questions kept over time, each judged on the facts that bear on it, in a library that already exists when news arrives. I would change this if he says a cold start on two weeks of news is itself the product.

**Is it a measuring problem?** Largely yes. Since 11-05 every test starts empty, so it scores whether two weeks of passing mentions re-create the key's exact questions; both systems get 1–2 of 7 while "no eligible judgement disagrees" (CMP). The lines are finer than the readers and the model's own spread. Two defects are real under every instrument: indirect facts not delivered, and unstable question forming. A warm-start run with the same losses, or a human reader confirming the zero-fault failures, would change my mind.

**Why stuck, and what breaks through?** The loop tunes sentences in the one reading call against step counts; the judged result moved only when the judge was given more (questions, starting figures, delivered facts). Measure in the real condition, anchor the readers once to a person, and move delivery out of the one-pass reading. I would drop this if the carried-library comparison shows no gain, or if supplying the missing facts on fresh weeks leaves answers unchanged (the one six-call test, D511, was inconclusive).

## 7. A sound measurement: a card deck Alex marks

*(A proposal; the reading-time and availability figures are inference.)*

- **Material, all stored:** July runs c1–c3 and p1–p3 (`poc/data/clean-e2e-full-2026-11-13`), the week of 09-22 for both systems, the week of 10-06, and `side-by-side/build_side_by_side.py`. Its current page is 15,446 words *(my count)*, too long.

- **Marks:** about 40 cards, three ticks each: would I hold this question as worded; does the answer follow from what is shown; is something important missing or wrong.
- **Known error, built in:** six repeated cards (Alex's own consistency); pairs from two draws of the *same* system shown as "X against Y" (the noise floor); four planted wrong answers (sets exist from Stage B and the week). The two model families mark the same deck first, so their agreement with Alex becomes their measured error.
- **Accumulates:** the matter list only grows; each new version is re-rendered on it; Alex's marks are frozen as the reference, corrected by dated records.
- **Second key that grows by itself:** later stored news (items run to 10-27, LEAN-LOG §1) shows which way July's answers should have leaned. Availability per question not checked.
- **Cost:** $0 model spend; builder work; reader sessions (unpriced); one hour of Alex per round.
- **Cannot show:** whether 2027 answers come true; anything beyond NVDA and three windows; differences under roughly 20–30 points on 40 cards (D517's arithmetic applies); matters nobody listed; which step caused a bad card.

## D198 · 2026-10-27 · A judgement reads the evidence in view, not everything in force

- Alex, 2026-10-27, on the finding that evidence in force grows without bound (v6, NVIDIA FY2027 Data Center revenue: 574 pieces after six weeks, 415 never cited by any of its 33 judgements; 40 of 316 judge requests over 30k tokens, max 67k; judging 38% of spend and rising; the run's stall came from enumerating 300+ ids): "这是什么问题你深度思考之后改".
- What the problem is (design: `docs/research/2026-10-27-evidence-in-view/design.md`): two mechanisms. (1) Extraction links wide: `role-v14.txt` says "every statement and number is, by default, evidence linked to a shown thesis" and also "link only to the thesis it directly concerns; omit statements with no thesis"; the model attaches every business mention to the broadest thesis (2.5 pieces per item on v6; a liquid-cooling note, a SuperPOD purchase, a rack R&D story). Not changed here; the prompt audit is reported to Alex as the next slice. (2) Judging-v4 reads everything in force every time ("Rejudge from all evidence currently in force"); an analyst keeps what his view rests on and reads what arrived.
- Decided: from judging-v5 (`poc-v30`) a judgement of a thesis is shown, of its evidence in force, the arrivals (pieces linked after the thesis's fifth most recent judgement, READINGS = 5; everything when it has fewer) and the basis (pieces cited by one of its last ten judgements, BASIS = 10). The rest stays in force in the ledger; the request names the count ("[Not shown: N more pieces in force, read in earlier judgements; the previous conclusion carries them]"); the answer may cite and push only shown ids, checked against the request that was sent (`judging.evidence_shown_in`, as the theme block is). Nothing leaves the ledger; the repeat / replace / new rules, "in force", the rejudgement triggers, eligibility, the theme block and dependencies are unchanged. Gated on the prompt version: v4 ledgers and configurations read in force as before.
- Measured ($0, `census.py`, two ledgers): among judgements after a thesis's first, the rule would have hidden 1.5% (nvda-3m) and 1.1% (r5) of the citations the judge actually made (22 of 325 and 7 of 261 judgements lose one cite, mostly third-party risk mentions listed in a "pull the other way" sentence); shown mean 95 and 109 pieces where in force averaged 225 and 178. Tighter rules hid 16% (cited last time + new since) or kept growing (ever cited + three readings). Arm beside control (`ab.py`, $0.03): v6, v11, v22 from the same ledger state, v4 fresh against v5: the same rung and `changed` on all three, reasons consistent, request tokens 76,476 → 12,516, 53,151 → 11,204, 25,806 → 8,425. Tests: `tests/test_evidence_in_view.py` (4, red first); suite 199.
- Applied to the three-month run at a day boundary: 2026-08-18 finished under `poc-v29` on the serial path (the parallel runner refuses a half-done day after a code change), `poc-v30` from 2026-08-19. Prompt `judging-v5` is `judging-v4` with the first rule reworded (2,264 → 2,437 characters; the growth is the sentence that says what is not shown and who carries it).
- Also in this slice, from the stall at 2026-08-07: a code-refused judgement answer is retired from the archive's lookup (`model.Archive.retire`; the row stays; schema-refused and malformed rows already carried a suffix), so a resume re-samples instead of replaying the refused answer; and the request's closing line names a closed set that exists ("cites_views must be empty: this thesis depends on no other thesis"; "a theme id goes only in theme_pushes, never in cites or cites_views"): 4 of the run's 5 retried first answers had put theme ids into cites_views.

`../reflection-3/cold-codex-4.md` (the test and its five proofs) and `cold-codex-5.md` (consensus).

## What it asks

Every clean measurement examined so far starts from an empty library. In the week of 10-06 that produced 13 topics, 12 of
them (by both reader families) on matters that already existed, some of which the same system had opened two weeks earlier
in its own run of the week of 09-22. The record of 2026-11-05 asks for a test that starts from a library built from real
material available before the test. This comparison is the smallest form of it: does the unchanged first step, shown the
library it built itself in the week of 09-22, stop re-creating the questions that library holds, without losing the
article's facts or the questions that are really new?

## What is sent

- The unchanged first step (`clean-arch/step1/run_live.py`; DeepSeek flash, high effort, the frozen request).
- The 11 distinct articles from which the stored October run opened its 13 topics (`inputs/articles.json`; selected because
  they opened topics: this is not a sample of the week's news).
- Each article is read twice, each read its own one-article run from a fixed starting library: `empty`
  (`inputs/initial-empty.json`) and `carried` (`inputs/initial-carried.json`: the seven topics of the September run's completed
  state). 22 reads, one draw, two at a time, on one new ledger with a ceiling of $1.00. Driver: `run_probe.py`.
- Size: the $0 dry run charged $0.46 for the 22 reads at the stored answers' sizes (the ledger's prices); the stored run needed
  14 calls for these 11 articles (three resends), so about $0.5 is expected. An estimate, not a measurement.

## The reading (fixed now)

Alex's rule of 2026-11-05, applied to the library actually shown: a matter the library already holds, not opened again, is
correct; a matter it lacks and that is worth a question, opened, is correct; whether the existing question received the
article's facts is checked apart.

1. Claude reads every one of the 22 answers beside its article and stores its marks first. Then two reader families apart,
   with the article, the open questions shown and the answer.
2. Per new topic in an answer: `redundant` (the library shown holds the same question), `related` (it holds the same matter
   in another shape), `new`; and whether it is worth a question by the standard's test for a big matter.
3. Per labelled case: the article's statements on that matter in each read: kept and filed under the existing question,
   kept and filed elsewhere or nowhere, or not kept. The empty read of the same article is the reference for what was there
   to keep.
4. The five absent cases are the guard against suppression: opened or not in each read.

**It supports going on** when, on the same-question cases, the carried read opens no second question on the matter and files
under the existing one at least what the empty read kept, and the absent cases open as often as in the empty read.
**It fails** when the carried read re-opens the same question in two or more of the four same-question cases; or drops the
matter's statements where the empty read kept them, in two or more; or opens two or fewer of the absent cases that the empty
read opens. Anything between is reported as it is. Ambiguous coverage stays unresolved. One draw: a reason to go on or to
stop, not an estimate of anything.

**Stopping rule of the run:** the first read the ledger refuses, that fails in transport after its retries, or whose launcher
prints no result stops the probe; an answer the step's own checks reject is that read's outcome.

## The classes, by mechanism

1. **Five states for an event are where the step is weakest.** 15 of 17 company five-state ladders are unsound as ruled, 10
   by both readers. The states leave a case out or let two hold (a prohibition in force while a review is pending; "broad"
   against "narrower" with no line), the labels run against the business (an investigation that lapses with no fine labelled
   Strongly bearish), the Neutral state names no baseline, and a regulator's decision is filed under the company in one send
   and under the theme in the next. Seven theses change shape between sends (yes/no in one, five states in another).
2. **A yes/no whose Yes needs a confirmation and whose No does not** (3 as ruled, 1 by both): shipped and not yet confirmed
   fits neither rung.

### Dry run of the Stage A reading ($0): done in this review

`dryrun/` holds 18 hand-written ladders as the judge would be shown them: 7 written to be sound, one of each answer shape and a
justified refusal, and 11 each carrying one planted fault: one under each of ten marks, two under R and none under XR (`build_dryrun.py`; the key stayed outside the
repository until both readers had answered). Two readers of different families marked them blind with the Stage A form
(`reader-brief.md`; `score_dryrun.py`).

| | reader 1 (Codex family) | reader 2 (Claude family) |
|---|---|---|
| planted faults caught under their own mark | 11 of 11 | 11 of 11 |
| sound ladders given a failed mark | 3 of 7 | 0 of 7 |
| time for the 18 ladders | 25 seconds | 293 seconds |

- **Every planted fault was caught under its own mark by both readers.** That is ten of the eleven marks: XR had no planted
  fault, here or in any later reading. Readers have failed XR four times on answers I had written as sound (this reading's
  item 1, the sixth's item 1, the eighth's item 2, the eleventh's item 12), which shows that they use the mark and not how often they would catch a
  planted fault under it.
- **A planted fault often breaks more than one mark.** Readers failed further marks on some planted answers of the first two
  readings (a wrong due day also fails Q; a misplaced reference also fails G); the record below lists each.
- **The record of every reading is `readings_summary.md`,** generated by `readings_summary.py` from the stored answers: every
  failed mark and every fault named under `W`, by reader and item, and for the first two readings the planted mark beside it.
  The accounts below interpret that record and must agree with it.
- **The three marks reader 1 failed on my "sound" ladders were right:** two five-state ladders did not cover every outcome or let
  two states hold at once, and one reference quoted talks, which are not an expectation. The fixtures in

way to keep them short is to write the counting for "kept and linked" and for the readers at the first draft, where arm c1 had failed.
- **Step one's result (D491; `main-numbers/RESULT.md`, `tally-stage1.txt`):** 60 valid sends, $1.02. Against the control: the three questions
  open (fiscal 2027 revenue 9 of 9, the fiscal 2028 margin 6 of 6, fiscal 2028 revenue 13 of 15 with the growth shape disputed by the
  readers), figures kept and linked, no number card, none twice, none from a bare figure; statements with no question 118 → 45.
  **Fails on suppression:** the Vera Rubin question 0 of 3 against c8's 2 of 3. The hypothesis is refuted on a condition written beforehand;
  the line stops (D355).
- **Council round 16** (`mw-codex-16.md`): the verdict stands; my "the revenue question caused it" was a lead stated as a cause: the reasoning
  also gives the missing shipment date, as c8's non-opening send does. Not shown: that revenue must swallow product questions, or that
  statements without a figure never belong under revenue.
- **Where kept figures stand ($0):** 382 of 567 statements in the judge's store have no question; the 70% outlook is in none of 37 judgement
  requests; later linking judged 516 earlier statements and linked 2.
- *Lessons:*
  - The stop condition written before the send did its work: the arm passed every line it was built for and would have gone on to a paid
    week on those alone.
  - Read a reasoning trace for every reason it gives, not for the one that fits the story: I quoted the sentences that filed the news
    under revenue and passed over the date sentences beside them. The council read all three and found both.
  - Three sends a case can stop a line; they cannot name its cause. A cause needs either the control's spread or a case built to split
    the two reasons.

docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-4/codex-design.md:46:## 6. My answers to Alex’s three questions
docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-4/codex-design.md:48:**What are we trying to achieve?** A dependable, evolving research record that lets an analyst see important questions, the evidence behind them, and a defensible current answer. I would revise that description if Alex intends the product to make a narrower decision or to replace a specific part of an analyst’s workflow rather than support the whole record. ([clean PRD §1](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/PRD.md:5))
docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-4/codex-design.md:50:**Is measurement part of the problem?** Yes: the current checks provide useful evidence but do not yet establish the complete user outcome, and empty-start results answer a different question from behavior with an established library. The second-week review also exposed reader disagreement, including conflicting instructions about a due date; this is evidence to resolve the measurement procedure, not grounds to erase the failed gate. ([second-week result](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/second-week/RESULT.md:117); [D559](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS.md:903))
docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-4/codex-design.md:52:**What could break the impasse?** My recommendation is the already proposed small comparison of the same articles with a verified prior library and with an empty start, reading the resulting questions and evidence delivery against the actual state shown. It would change my mind if the carried library produces the same material failures, or introduces offsetting duplicates or missed evidence; even a positive result would be a diagnostic, not production acceptance. The recorded next step waits for Alex’s confirmation and authorization. ([D559](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS.md:903); [CURRENT_STATE](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/CURRENT_STATE.md:273))

# The small comparison D559 puts to Alex: the week of 10-06's opening articles read from a kept library and from empty (not started), 2026-11-15

**Status: prepared and proved at $0; nothing is sent without Alex's word.** Decision D559; council
`../reflection-3/cold-codex-4.md` (the test and its five proofs) and `cold-codex-5.md` (consensus).

## What it asks

Every clean measurement examined so far starts from an empty library. In the week of 10-06 that produced 13 topics, 12 of
them (by both reader families) on matters that already existed, some of which the same system had opened two weeks earlier
in its own run of the week of 09-22. The record of 2026-11-05 asks for a test that starts from a library built from real
material available before the test. This comparison is the smallest form of it: does the unchanged first step, shown the
library it built itself in the week of 09-22, stop re-creating the questions that library holds, without losing the
article's facts or the questions that are really new?

## What is sent

- The unchanged first step (`clean-arch/step1/run_live.py`; DeepSeek flash, high effort, the frozen request).
- The 11 distinct articles from which the stored October run opened its 13 topics (`inputs/articles.json`; selected because
  they opened topics: this is not a sample of the week's news).
- Each article is read twice, each read its own one-article run from a fixed starting library: `empty`
  (`inputs/initial-empty.json`) and `carried` (`inputs/initial-carried.json`: the seven topics of the September run's completed
  state). 22 reads, one draw, two at a time, on one new ledger with a ceiling of $1.00. Driver: `run_probe.py`.
- Size: the $0 dry run charged $0.46 for the 22 reads at the stored answers' sizes (the ledger's prices); the stored run needed
  14 calls for these 11 articles (three resends), so about $0.5 is expected. An estimate, not a measurement.

Frozen inputs:
- `inputs/articles.json`: sha256 `6ead553882e3c430…`
- `inputs/initial-carried.json`: sha256 `6e0669faac176a63…`
- `inputs/initial-empty.json`: sha256 `37517e5f3dc66819…`
- `inputs/manifest-base.json`: sha256 `3038c186e9a05d59…`
- `inputs/settings.json`: sha256 `7716a85da8750830…`

## Proved at $0 (`proofs/`)

| Proof | What it shows | Judged | Mutant that must fail |
|---|---|---|---|
| `carried_library_proof.py` E1 | the carried library is the September run's completed state: started from empty, every article complete, the state after the last one, equal to that run's seven topics, window ending 2026-09-28 | 235 articles, 7 topics | a dropped topic: fails |
| E2 | the articles are the opening articles of the October week's 13 topics, in reading order, each equal to its stored case | 13 topics, 11 articles | a swapped article: fails |
| E3 | the real run loop, given an article's stored library, rebuilds the stored request byte for byte and the same library after | 11 of 11 | |
| E4 | an empty-start request equals a stored one as built | 1 | |
| E5 | the carried request differs from the empty one only in the open questions shown, which are the September state's | 11 of 11 pairs | |
| E6 | the same settings and system text in both stored runs and today | 2 runs | |
| `probe_dry_run_proof.py` D1 to D3 | the real driver and launcher under the trap (canned answers, placeholder keys): 22 reads, 22 sends each under a live reservation; requests stored with the intended open questions; the bytes sent from empty for the article production itself read from empty equal the bytes production sent; ledger 22 attempts, none refused, nothing left reserved | 22 reads | |
| D4 | with a ceiling below one reservation the first read is refused, the ledger stops, the probe stops, no send | 1 run | a driver that ignores the stop: fails |

Not proved by these: anything about what the model will answer. The dry run's answers were written for another library and
are not results.

## The cases, labelled before any answer (against the carried library alone)

From the two reader families' coverage answers (`../reflection-3/codex-coverage.jsonl`, `claude-coverage.jsonl`: the September
topics they named for each October topic) and my own read stored before theirs.

| October topic (stored run) | Article (sequence) | Against the carried library |
|---|---|---|
| clean-2 supply commitments | 9 | same question (September clean-2), both families |
| clean-5 the Hugging Face acquisition | 30 | same question (September clean-6), both |
| clean-7 Rubin's ramp | 76 | same question (September clean-4), both; the deadline is worded differently |
| clean-4 capital spending 2026 and 2027 | 15 | 2026 is September clean-5 (both); 2027 is not in the carried library |
| clean-1 the lease guarantee | 9 | related: September clean-1 asks the total of credit support, both |
| clean-8 the loss-share exposure | 76 | related: September clean-1, both |
| clean-6 the U.S. licence requirement | 35 | unresolved: one family names September clean-3 |
| clean-12 global AI spending | 206 | unresolved: one family names September clean-5 |
| clean-3 memory prices, clean-9 Groq's rack, clean-10 the B200 rental price, clean-11 Reflection AI, clean-13 the equity commitments | 12, 119, 173, 200, 235 | absent |

## The reading (fixed now)

Alex's rule of 2026-11-05, applied to the library actually shown: a matter the library already holds, not opened again, is
correct; a matter it lacks and that is worth a question, opened, is correct; whether the existing question received the
article's facts is checked apart.

1. Claude reads every one of the 22 answers beside its article and stores its marks first. Then two reader families apart,
   with the article, the open questions shown and the answer.
2. Per new topic in an answer: `redundant` (the library shown holds the same question), `related` (it holds the same matter
   in another shape), `new`; and whether it is worth a question by the standard's test for a big matter.
3. Per labelled case: the article's statements on that matter in each read: kept and filed under the existing question,
   kept and filed elsewhere or nowhere, or not kept. The empty read of the same article is the reference for what was there
   to keep.
4. The five absent cases are the guard against suppression: opened or not in each read.

**It supports going on** when, on the same-question cases, the carried read opens no second question on the matter and files
under the existing one at least what the empty read kept, and the absent cases open as often as in the empty read.
**It fails** when the carried read re-opens the same question in two or more of the four same-question cases; or drops the
matter's statements where the empty read kept them, in two or more; or opens two or fewer of the absent cases that the empty
read opens. Anything between is reported as it is. Ambiguous coverage stays unresolved. One draw: a reason to go on or to
stop, not an estimate of anything.

**Stopping rule of the run:** the first read the ledger refuses, that fails in transport after its retries, or whose launcher
prints no result stops the probe; an answer the step's own checks reject is that read's outcome.

## To start it (only on Alex's word)

```
python3 clean-arch/e2e-comparison-2026-11-13/budget_replay.py --init-ledger <root>/ledger.json --ceiling 1.00
caffeinate -i python3 docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-library/run_probe.py --root <root>/reads --ledger <root>/ledger.json
```

# Can an affordable comparison tell the two systems apart? The sizing (D516, under D439), 2026-11-15, $0

**Answer: at the proposed size the comparison may miss differences that matter, and its reliability cannot yet be calculated from the
stored readings. It was not run.** Under simple assumptions (independent answers, the fresh week's question counts, the shares seen
so far) the smallest difference such a comparison would detect four times in five is between about 22 and 38 points for the shapes
the money allows, and more if repeated draws add little; these are illustrations, not a measured boundary. The differences seen so
far are 6, 19 and 26 points on one run each, which neither establish the true differences nor rule out larger ones. By the stop
condition written in D516 this design is not sent. That stops this design at this size; it does not show that the systems are
equal, or that no comparison could ever decide.

Scripts: `draw_counts.py` (what each stored draw holds, by code; `draw-counts.json`), `sizing.py` (the calculation, its inputs printed
with their sources, the closed form checked by simulation).

What this table says before any calculation:

## 2. How large a difference a comparison could detect

Inputs (all from the fresh week, and all estimates): at the end of one week the new system holds 7 questions with a latest answer
and the old system 15; a week costs about $2.52 a draw for the new system (charged) and about $0.50 for the old (its token count at
listed rates, rounded up; not a separately charged amount). The article database holds articles for three later weeks (2026-10-06
to 10-26); **no exposure census has been run on them and no article list priced**, so their being unread and their cost are
assumptions here. The week of 09-29 has 40 articles already read once by the reading step.

The smallest true difference detected four times in five (two-sided, 5%):

| Shape | Cost | Answers supported | Trivia or duplicates |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 week, 3 draws each | about $9 | 31 points if repeated draws were as good as new weeks; 54 if they add nothing | 34; 60 |
| 2 weeks, 3 draws each | about $18 | 22; 38 | 24; 42 |
| 3 weeks, 1 draw each | about $9 | 31 | 34 |
| 3 weeks, 2 draws each | about $18 | 22; 31 | 24; 34 |
| 4 weeks, 3 draws each (more unread news and money than there is) | about $36 | 16; 27 | 17; 30 |

- The calculation assumes independent answers, fixed weekly question counts and particular starting shares. Questions within a
  week, and repeated draws of the same week, are correlated to a degree the stored runs do not measure for these readings. "As good
  as new weeks" is an upper bound on what repeated draws can give.
- The simulation checks the formula under the same assumptions; it does not validate the assumptions. For 3 weeks and 1 draw (21
  and 45 answers): a 31-point difference is detected in 82% of 20,000 simulated comparisons, a 10-point difference in 12%, and a
  20-point difference in roughly 40 to 60% depending on the starting shares (about 37% at 83 against 63, about 57% at 97 against
  77, the council's own runs).
- Big matters covered cannot be sized this way at all: a week gives two to seven such matters.

## 3. The stop condition of D516, applied

- **A stated difference the comparison is meant to detect:** none can be defended. Under the simple assumptions the shapes the
  money allows detect differences of roughly 22 to 38 points or more; one draw of each system does not tell us whether the true
  differences are that large (the largest seen is 26 points, on one week), and on the one line with two windows the sign flips.
- **A defensible size and cost for it:** the reliability of a $9 to $18 comparison cannot be calculated from the stored readings
  (no repeated draws of the reader-based lines; correlation unmeasured). Spending the remaining money on a test whose power is
  unknown and plausibly low is not defensible.
- **The readers' controls:** the delivery reading still has no known single-fact "would change" case (the six calls of D511 did not
  give one), so that line could not be exercised either.
- **So this design is not sent.** What is unmeasured and would have to change for a comparison to decide: many more independent
  weeks of unread news than the database holds (seven to nine weeks for a 20-point difference at one draw each), or a line that does
  not depend on the handful of questions a week produces.

## 4. What this means for the decision page

The page's section 5 offered Alex "one comparison written down before it runs" as the way to choose by measurement. The page now
says, in plain words: at the proposed size the comparison may miss differences that matter; we cannot yet calculate its
reliability from our stored readings; we did not run it.

**I agree that measurement is a major reason the work has stalled, but I would not yet say it is the main cause.** The strongest counterexample is that real product failures remain even when readers agree: the same news produced questions with different scopes, and a later test declined both years of cloud spending in all three attempts. A better test may show those failures matter less than the current gate suggests; it cannot make them disappear. [D559]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:6976), [October result]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/second-week/RESULT.md)

**(a) “Largely the measuring, not only.”** I would say **“both, with measurement preventing us from knowing how much each contributes.”** The gate has substantial reader disagreement, no demonstrated reference set that clears the whole gate, and no measured effect of fixing its failures on the final answer. But the agreed question and refusal faults are evidence against attributing most of the delay to measurement alone. [First-gate map]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/second-week/FIRST-GATE-MAP.md), [D467–D468]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS.md:811)

Your control finding needs a narrower sentence. The old system’s 36 answer-choice lists were **different questions**, and each reader separately found firm faults on some; that is a useful warning, not a same-population test proving no good system can clear the six lines. The seven allegedly sound examples also were not established as sound: the design itself says its author’s examples were not reliably sound. [Stage A result]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/stage_a/result/RESULT.md:55), [design]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/DESIGN.md:1046)

**(b) “What the judge is given, never wording” is selection.** D263 is a direct counterexample: changing the judge’s wording moved six of seven re-sent cases into the reference ranges. It is weak evidence of general improvement because the added instructions were derived from those same reference answers, and the record says a full end-to-end run was still needed. [D263]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:3069)

There is also evidence against **delivery alone** as the breakthrough. In the later direct-source test, operating margin agreed 3/3 and capital spending 2/3, but custom chips agreed only **1/3**; the independent reading found unsupported reasoning in all three custom-chip answers. This is distinct from the earlier 9/9 movement off the lowest range: moving an answer and making it sound are different results. [Filing log, rows 20–22]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-04-filing-end-to-end/log.md:24)

The defensible claim is: **giving the judge a better starting state or missing facts produced some of the clearest measured changes; wording also changed results, sometimes with regressions or reference-fitting.** The seeded 18/18/17 versus 17/15/16 result was registered as inconclusive, and the seeded-versus-unseeded comparison used different days. [Step 1 log]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step1-unfiled-2026-11-08/LOG.md:2531)

**(c) The gate.** You may recommend changing its role, but D400’s acceptance makes the lines Alex’s decision, even though you proposed them. D484 added a use-oriented acceptance beside the existing gates; it did not demote them. [D400]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:4376), [gate frame]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/NEW-SYSTEM-FRAME.md:19)

The sentence to Alex should be:

> “Should the six answer-choice lines remain a required gate, or should we keep their failures visible as diagnostics and decide readiness using a product-level review with controls; I recommend the latter once that review has been tested?”

Do not call the card deck a replacement for the **frozen** reference: that requires a separate decision, and the frozen files stay unchanged.

**(d) The deck.** It is a promising **pilot of a review method**, not yet a sound instrument or a basis for ranking systems. I would use 12–16 distinct, preselected cards plus 3–4 hidden repeats, balanced across systems and including known missing questions, a clearly supported answer and independently checked wrong answers. The two model families mark the identical, blinded cards first; Alex then marks each **worth tracking / answer supported / cannot tell**, with a brief reason and the actual material available through a link.

Cut the claim that three selected passages can establish “nothing important is missing.” They can show whether those passages support an answer; they cannot show what the selector omitted. For a small preselected subset, give Alex a separately prepared source comparison, including a known consequential omission and a negative control; otherwise mark completeness **not assessed**. Allow opening sources: needing them is normal research, not failure of the method.

The main trap is **selection bias**: a neat card can make a weak answer look convincing, and cards drawn only from opened questions hide the questions never opened. Repeated identical cards measure Alex’s consistency on those cases; two draws of the same system show output variation, not his error rate. Agreement with Alex is agreement with his judgement, not a measured ground truth. Thirty minutes, costs and reliability need to be timed and measured; the prior trial’s 25 minutes was model-reader time. [Use-oriented trial]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/TRIAL-RESULT.md)

**(e) Order.** Put the **$0 deck pilot first**, then D559’s carried-library comparison, using the pilot to make its reading clear. D559 is a focused and already prepared test of a different question—whether an existing library reduces redundant openings without losing facts or worthwhile questions—not a system ranking or a test of final-answer quality. Its proposed **11 articles × two conditions**, one draw, costs about **$0.50 estimated**, with a $1 ceiling; the decision record says it awaits Alex’s confirmation. A deck of July empty-start outputs cannot answer the starting-library question either. [D559]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:6976), [decision page]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/DECISION-PAGE-2026-11-15.md:274)

I would **size retrieval as a candidate**, not decide now that the answering step must search. The 389 unlinked statements are not 389 proven omissions: the later census found **three confirmed missing fact–question pairs and 23 unresolved**, and the six-call effect test was inconclusive. Retrieval can introduce irrelevant, repeated or outdated facts and must be tested for those harms as well as recovery. D198’s reason for restricting what the judge sees was a real cost and context problem. [Week result]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/week/WEEK-RESULT.md:20), [D508–D514]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS.md:852), [D198]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:2559)

**(f) Other corrections.** The history report’s “about fifteen candidates” and “about twenty instruments” are its counts, not a verified census I can independently endorse. Its “no library ever carried” also needs the scope D559 uses: **the clean measurements examined**, not every run in project history. [History report]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-4/claude-history.md), [D559]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:6976)

The existing page server does accept a database path, but that alone does not prove the saved clean run renders correctly in the product page, nor that Alex has never inspected it. Treat both as unverified until the page and his interaction are checked. [Page server]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/scripts/hivemind_api.py:22)

**The three answers to Alex:**

1. **The goal:** a continuing research library in which an analyst can find important questions, the facts for and against them, and a current answer whose reasons are visible. I would change this if Alex specifies a narrower job for the product. [Clean PRD]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/PRD.md:7)
2. **Is measurement the problem?** It is a major part of the impasse, alongside demonstrated product defects; we cannot yet apportion the blame. A controlled review that separates reliable product failures from reader and sampling variation would change that assessment.
3. **Why stuck, and how through?** Too many local pass/fail decisions have been made without a reliable connection to what the analyst sees, while important facts and answerable questions still go missing.
